subject: Bridgelink: intermittent token bursts & websocket churn impacting investor demo

Subject: Live demo — repeated short bursts, WS disconnects (urgent)

Hi Logan / Karthik,

We hit a problem during a live investor demo about 8 minutes in. The model output started arriving in very short bursts (a few tokens at a time), then long gaps, and finally the WebSocket disconnected twice. When the connection was live the latency for some responses spiked to several seconds.

I attached the capture and a list of request IDs we saw on our side. The investor call paused while we tried to reconnect — this is high severity for us. Can your team confirm whether this is a client-side keepalive issue or something on the Redwood service? Any immediate mitigation steps we should try?

We can share additional traces if needed.

- Alex
Bridgelink Labs
Product Lead

Attachments: bridgelink-demo-20270919-capture.log (text), sample-request-ids.txt

Subject: Re: Live demo — repeated short bursts, WS disconnects (urgent)

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm escalating this to on-call and SRE. Initial ack: we see a number of short-lived chunks in the capture and repeated websocket reconnects on your session IDs.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- SRE will fetch full traces for the request ids you sent and check proxy/edge error patterns.
- We'll attempt a targeted failover of the session to an isolated pool and re-run with a non-batched inference path to remove batching as a variable.
- Can you confirm whether your client sets a websocket-level ping/keepalive and the max message size? Also tell us if the demo used chunked transfer or streaming SSE (you noted websocket earlier).

I know this is urgent — I'm asking Grace from CS to offer a replacement slot for your demo if you'd like. Karthik, Soojin — please triage and post findings. I'll keep Alex and Susan updated every 30 minutes.

- Logan

Subject: Re: Live demo — repeated short bursts, WS disconnects (urgent)

Logan / team / Alex — quick triage notes after a first-pass on the captures you provided:

What I see:
- Multiple 502/504s at the edge for the session's request IDs during the 09:20–09:30 window. The pattern shows upstream queue growth on the serving pool and repeated connection resets from the proxy.
- Token output pattern looks like we shifted from continuous streaming to micro-batched flushes — likely the batching controller detected a slowdown and started emitting partial chunks rather than waiting for full batch completion.
- No obvious client-side keepalive failures in the websocket frames you sent — pings are present at 15s.

Temporary mitigations applied (09:55):
- We bumped the session to a high-priority routing policy to force route to a warm, dedicated pool.
- Disabled the adaptive batching controller for that routing path so the server will stream tokens immediately rather than waiting for batch windows.

Prelim conclusion:
- Root cause hypothesis: transient backpressure in the serving pool (GC or a slow kernel) that increased per-token latency; batching controller responded by shrinking emission windows, producing the 'staccato' token arrival you observed. The proxy then timed out idle frames causing reconnects.

Next asks:
1) Please share one affected request-id with full client-side frames (if possible).
2) Can we schedule a 30-minute postmortem call with Bridgelink Ops and our SREs at 11:30 PT?

I'll prepare traces and a short mitigation runbook.

- Soojin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. I attached one of the full captures with the websocket frames. The investor meeting ended up rescheduling; this is something we need to resolve before next week or it will affect our close.

A couple of clarifications:
- The demo used WebSocket streaming with per-token messages; keepalive pings are every 15s.
- We saw errors in the UI corresponding to 502 at the exact time of the long gaps.
- For the record, Bridgelink will expect a credit for the disruption if this is a server-side issue. Please advise on next steps and an ETA on a full postmortem.

Subject: Exec escalation: Bridgelink outage during demo — action & ask

Team — summary and ask:

Summary:
- Customer: Bridgelink Labs (BRG-4501). On 2027-09-19 their investor demo experienced intermittent micro-bursts of tokens and websocket disconnects. Initial SRE triage points to transient serving-pool backpressure that triggered adaptive batching to emit partial flushes; proxy idle timeouts then caused disconnects. Temporary mitigations (failover + disable adaptive batching) restored stable streaming.
- Business impact: demo delayed; customer requests credit and a written postmortem. They are contractually in a committed trial and are in late-stage procurement.

Immediate asks (for exec):
1) Marissa — please approve offering Bridgelink a one-month service credit as a gesture while we complete the postmortem.
2) Karthik / Soojin — produce a 72-hour postmortem draft with root cause, mitigation, and a two-week remediation plan (kernel-level patches, batching controller safeguard, routing policy hardening). Include performance regression tests.
3) Grace — coordinate a replacement demo slot for Bridgelink and own customer communications.

Mitigations already in flight:
- Forced routing to a warm pool per-session for impacted requests (done).
- Disabled adaptive batching for the Bridgelink routing policy (done).
- Collecting extended traces and kernel stats for the 09/19 window (SOON).

Timeline: postmortem draft in 72 hours (2027-09-24), remediation plan in two weeks (2027-10-05).

I'll patch this into the executive incident board and keep Alex informed. Rafael, please loop Legal/Finance if a formal credit memo is required.

- Logan
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
